problem.problem:
Anne is cold. Anne is furry. Anne is not quiet. Charlie is kind. Fiona is not quiet. Fiona is young. Harry is cold. Kind things are furry. Nice things are big. Furry things are nice. If something is young and furry then it is quiet. If Anne is quiet then Anne is cold. Kind, big things are young. If something is kind and not furry then it is not young.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Charlie is not furry.
raw_logic_programs:
Predicates:
Cold($x, bool) ::: Is x cold?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Kind($x, bool) ::: Is x kind?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Nice($x, bool) ::: Is x nice?
Big($x, bool) ::: Is x big?

Facts:
Cold(Anne, True) ::: Anne is cold.
Furry(Anne, True) ::: Anne is furry.
Quiet(Anne, False) ::: Anne is not quiet.
Kind(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is kind.
Quiet(Fiona, False) ::: Fiona is not quiet.
Young(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is young.
Cold(Harry, True) ::: Harry is cold.

Rules:
Kind($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Kind things are furry.
Nice($x, True) >>> Big($x, True) ::: Nice things are big.
Furry($x, True) >>> Nice($x, True) ::: Furry things are nice.
Young($x, True) && Furry($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, True) ::: If something is young and furry then it is quiet.
Quiet(Anne, True) >>> Cold(Anne, True) ::: If Anne is quiet then Anne is cold.
Kind($x, True) && Big($x, True) >>> Young($x, True) ::: Kind, big things are young.
Kind($x, True) && Furry($x, False) >>> Young($x, False) ::: If something is kind and not furry then it is not young.

Query:
Furry(Charlie, False) ::: Charlie is not furry.
